narrative.overview:
Money Stalker combines familiar account organization with expressive financial typography and a curious eye companion. The approved composition uses white top navigation, a deep ultramarine account rail, a primary ledger, and a right evidence/category workspace. The citron available amount is its financial focal point. The user rejected the earlier generic pastel helper-card treatment.

The eye helps orient, inspect evidence, and acknowledge completed review. Financial labels and warnings stay literal; the interface represents recorded data and explicit user decisions. Spanish copy, COP formatting, and America/Bogota dates give the workspace its local context.
keyCharacteristics: Grouped accounts and cards with readable balances and debt.
One self-hosted variable family, heavy headings, and tabular figures.
Blue actions, a citron available total, and textual semantic states.
Flat white work surfaces, fine borders, and native controls.

rules.name: The Explicit State Rule
rules.body: Pair status color with literal text and, where present, an icon. Color never carries the entire meaning alone.

rules.name: The Global Amount Rule
rules.body: Keep the citron amount explicitly labeled as available across all accounts. Account selection scopes activity and category spending, while the global amount remains global.

rules.name: The Complete Amount Rule
rules.body: Preserve the currency sign, grouping, and complete amount as a readable unit. At the narrowest breakpoint, reflow comparisons before squeezing figures; exceptionally long totals can scroll within their own amount region.

rules.name: The Flat Workspace Rule
rules.body: Group routine content with border, tone, and spacing. Reserve the shipped overlay shadow for modal elevation.

rules.name: The Evidence Review Rule
rules.body: Lead with focused evidence and compact durable progress. On phones, expand the group switcher only when needed. Accept localized COP searches, distinguish unmatched from incomplete evidence, and identify correction records before undo. Capture setup ends with verifying actual evidence received, not token creation.

rules.name: The Separate Holdings Rule
rules.body: Cash withdrawals transfer bank money to cash without new spending. Pocket and investment balances stay outside global available money and inside net worth. Investment values are manually declared, dated and reversible; value adjustments never count as liquid income or expense. Compatible SMS can transfer automatically into an owned pocket or investment only with an exact source, an unambiguous configured destination, complete consistent values and no possible prior match. Manual investment contributions offer existing products or inline creation named after the merchant by default. An explicit remember option applies the merchant category and investment destination to future CSV/XLSX previews; confirmation preserves the preview classification.

rules.name: The Financial Trail Rule
rules.body: Use the shared EvidenceTrail funds, evidence and holdings variants in reserved headings, empty states and beside the tilted rail eye companion. Keep motifs faint, static, noninteractive and aria-hidden. Never place decoration over amounts, rows, forms or statuses. Omit heading motifs at the narrowest widths. Pocket and investment products use their own semantic icons.

rules.name: The Product Setup Rule
rules.body: Configure SMS identity when creating or editing each non-cash product. Bank creation offers an optional debit card saved atomically with the same bank balance. Keep later debit creation available, personalization collapsed, and the shared four-step iPhone connection separate from product identity. Alias status never claims connected capture.

rules.name: The iPhone Form Rule
rules.body: Contain native date/time widths with min-inline-size zero and keep the native picker. Phone inputs and selects use 16px text and 44px targets. Remove nested product-editor indentation, wrap long names and actions, and give balances their own row. Stack report dates below 420px and wrap preset buttons. Never hide document overflow to conceal defects. Verify in local WebKit at 320–430px.

rules.name: The Mobile Ledger Rule
rules.body: Reserve 18px side gutters independently of generic scroll-table styling. Mobile grid rows keep merchant and complete amount above full-width notes and metadata. Stack amounts below merchants at 360px and narrower. Long text wraps, separators span the inset content width, and desktop preserves table columns. Keep a single instance of row details and retain accessible edit actions.

rules.name: The Captured Location Rule
rules.body: Send optional rich location inside the same capture-events request. Display address, coordinates, sample timestamp and unknown precision honestly. The primary MapLibre map distinguishes blue phone evidence from green owner-confirmed places; provider failures retain text and coordinate links to Apple Maps and Google Maps. Keep attribution visible and postal components collapsed. Location never proves merchant identity or blocks financial saving.

dos: **Do** reuse live tokens, shared primitives, and the catalog before adding a visual variant.
**Do** preserve white top navigation, the ultramarine hierarchy, heavy Inter headings, and the citron global available amount.
**Do** use tabular COP figures, explicit financial scope, and complete amounts at narrow widths.
**Do** pair status color with text and distinguish stale/incomplete data from an empty state.
**Do** preserve native controls, visible focus, accessible labels, and reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** update the catalog, this reference, and its sidecar when a repeated pattern enters the shared system.
donts: **Don't** replace the approved hierarchy with the rejected generic pastel helper-card composition.
**Don't** give debit instruments separate balances or make associated credit debt look like shared cash.
**Don't** imply bank synchronization, autonomous matching, or complete evidence through visual state or copy.
**Don't** ship example balances, fabricated analytics, unverified bank logos, or raster interface panels as real product data or UI.
**Don't** add decorative shadows to routine panels or replace the display family without an approved system change.
**Don't** clip, split, or hide a financial amount to preserve a desktop row on a narrow screen.
